scope.flow: EIP-712 off-chain intent signature verification and deposit
scope.environment: blockchain after chain fork / chain ID change
evidence: The `TrailsIntentEntrypoint` contract computes its EIP-712 `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR` once in the constructor and stores it as an immutable value:
Because `block.chainid` is read once at deployment, the stored `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR` permanently embeds the original chain ID.
If the chain later forks or the chain ID changes, this cached domain separator becomes outdated. As a result, the contract will continue validating signatures against an incorrect chain ID.
This causes all off-chain signatures to become invalid on the new chain, breaking signature-based flows such as `depositToIntent` and `depositToIntentWithPermit`.
Any signature generated on the new chain will not match the original domain separator. This creates a permanent denial-of-service for intent verification on the forked chain.
